question.:question/problem: Rewrite the expression $(x^{2} - 12x + 6^{2}) - 10$ as the difference between a perfect square and a constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}-2ax+{a}^{2}=(x-a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-12x+{6}^{2} & = \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+{6}^{2} & = \\ (x-6{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-12x+{6}^{2})-10 & = \\ (x-6{)}^{2}-10 & .\end{aligned}
$$
